::: {.hero-copy}
I am a physicist and PhD student in Computational Intelligence at the [Instituto de Investigación en Señales, Sistemas e Inteligencia Computacional (sinc(i))](https://sinc.unl.edu.ar/staff/guillermo-kulemeyer/), FICH-UNL-CONICET.

My research combines machine learning, bioinformatics, and statistical physics to study RNA secondary structures and biomolecular ensembles. I develop predictive models that infer structural properties from sequences and generative models that produce multiple plausible structures to represent diversity and uncertainty.

## Current Focus

::: {.focus-grid}
::: {.focus-item}
### Generative RNA Modeling

Conditional discrete diffusion models for sampling secondary structures and studying RNA ensembles beyond a single prediction.
:::

::: {.focus-item}
### Reliable Model Evaluation

Family-aware and sequence-similarity evaluation to understand how RNA prediction models generalize beyond familiar examples.
:::

::: {.focus-item}
### Teaching Neural Networks

Teaching Neural Networks I and II at FICH-UNL, connecting foundational concepts with modern deep-learning practice.
:::
:::

## Predictive and Generative Modeling

**Predictive modeling** estimates a structure or structural property from an RNA sequence. **Generative modeling** samples several plausible structures conditioned on that sequence, making it possible to study ensembles and uncertainty. My doctoral work examines both perspectives while keeping their aims and evaluation criteria distinct.
